fields.questionText: Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling white flame and changes into a white powder as shown in the diagram given below. The powder is dissolved in water. Identify the chemical formula of the white powder and the correct change observed when the solution is tested with litmus paper.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option: (b) — Mg burns in air to form MgO, which dissolves in water to give Mg(OH)2, a base; so the solution turns red litmus blue.

rationale: Figure (Mg ribbon burning, MgO in watch-glass) matches. Removed stray marks residue '1' but kept the figure reference since it is shown. Adopted fixer's subtopic and reasoned step; key (b) confirmed.

fields.questionText: A brooch is a decorative piece often worn on clothing like jackets, blouses or dresses to add elegance. Made from precious metals and decorated with gemstones, brooches come in many shapes and designs. One such brooch is made with silver wire in the form of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also used in making 5 diameters which divide the circle into 10 equal sectors as shown in the figure. Based on the above given information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the central angle of each sector. (ii) Find the length of the arc ACB. (iii) (a) Find the area of each sector of the brooch. OR (iii) (b) Find the total length of the silver wire used. (Use π = 22/7)
fields.answer: (i) 36° (ii) arc ACB = 11 mm (iii)(a) area of each sector = 385/4 = 96.25 mm² OR (iii)(b) total silver wire = 110 + 175 = 285 mm

rationale: Figure shows 10 equal sectors with A, C, B on one sector's arc — matches. Removed inline mark residues, kept 'as shown in the figure', rebuilt flattened answer. All values re-verified.

solved_answer: 2954 cm² if square corners (text); 2912 cm² if outer corners are quarter-circles r=7 — figure does not settle it
rationale: Figure shows a rounded-corner table but the inset corner looks square and no corner radius is given; text describes a plain rectangle (no circle content). Key still carries a 'pending verification' note. Cannot fix honestly.

fields.questionText: Colourless crystals of lead nitrate are heated strongly in a boiling tube as shown in the given figure. Identify the product which evolved during this reaction.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (b). On heating, lead nitrate decomposes: 2Pb(NO3)2(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO2(g) + O2(g). The brown fumes are of nitrogen dioxide (NO2); oxygen is colourless.

rationale: Figure shows heating of Pb(NO3)2 crystals with fumes — matches. Stem now names the reaction and points to the figure (requiresDiagram kept true); option letter prefixes removed. Key (b) unchanged.

solutionSteps: [1 mark] The shoot grows upwards, away from the root. The stimulus is light (positive phototropism); gravity (negative geotropism of the shoot) is also accepted.

rationale: Figure is a germinating seed with shoot growing up, root down; no light source drawn, so gravity is equally valid. Fixer's MCQ (Gravity as distractor, 'opening' setup) contradicts the figure. Kept VSA + figure; key accepts both.

fields.questionText: A potted plant is kept near a window. After a few days its shoot is seen bending towards the light coming in through the window. Explain how the plant hormone controls this growth response of the shoot.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The hormone auxin is synthesised at the shoot tip and diffuses down the shoot.
[1 mark] When light falls from one side, auxin collects on the side of the shoot away from the light (the shaded side).
[1 mark] Auxin causes the cells on the shaded side to elongate more, so that side grows faster and the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

solved_answer: Auxin made at shoot tip diffuses to shaded side, causing cell elongation there; shoot bends towards light.
rationale: Bound figure is a plain seedling (no light source, no bending, no auxin) — it does not illustrate the answer. Adopted fixer's self-contained 3-mark stem; figure binding should be dropped. Answer unchanged.

solved_answer: Part Y did not grow at all.
rationale: Figure clearly labels X (stem tip), Y (stem lower down), Z (roots), matching the stem; with the figure shown the row is answerable. Removing the auxin source stops elongation of Y. Key (c) correct; text rewrite unnecessary.

fields.questionText: Label the endocrine glands marked (a), (b), (c) and (d) in the given figure (Fig. 7.3).
fields.answer: (a) Pineal gland (b) Pituitary gland (c) Thyroid gland (d) Thymus
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) Pineal gland; (b) Pituitary gland — both in the brain.
[1 mark] (c) Thyroid gland (in the neck); (d) Thymus (in the upper chest).

rationale: Figure shows head/neck with 4 labels (a)-(d) only; served key listed adrenal, pancreas, gonads not in the figure. Rewrote key per NCERT Exemplar Q36 positions; a/b (pineal vs pituitary) worth a human glance.
